description: One HTML shell plus a JavaScript bundle; routing, rendering and data fetching happen in the browser and navigation never reloads the document.
The HTML is produced by JavaScript in the browser, so nothing meaningful is visible until the bundle runs.
Changes the URL and adds a history entry without loading a new document. Fires no event.
Fired on `window` when the user moves through history (back/forward) after the URL has changed.
A router calls `preventDefault()` on plain left clicks of its `<a>` elements and navigates itself; modified clicks are left to the browser.
Sequential loading: HTML, then the bundle, then a render, then a fetch, then another render. Each step waits for the previous one.
The host answers every unknown path with `index.html` (status 200) so the client router can render the page, including its own not-found screen.
